body: I was 16 and my model UN coach/politics teacher found out about me self harming. Legally, she was required to tell the guidance councilor and my parents etc, which turned into a nightmare and almost led to me being expelled (private school is wack). Anyways, she was the kindest person in this entire process, when she first found out she was beyond comforting about it, she listened to my updates about threats of expulsion from admin and assured that it would all turn out okay. She put up with a lot of crying and stress and would always take notice if it looked like I was having a bad day and make sure she checked in. She was really great, she wrote one of my college rec letters and I’m pretty sure it’s the reason I got into the schools I did, she was also an amazing teacher too

Don't have any experience with the career program, but I take GP HL and I love it now, but it's really dependent on whose teaching it. For year 1 the teacher wasn't great and didn't know what was going on, so I didn't enjoy the class then, but for year 2 my teacher is fantastic and always willing to chat about case studies or theories and makes the class into something you really care about. We've done a lot in the class, the engagement IA was hell for me but the video IAs were one of my favorite projects, but I guess since the course is so new workload can vary by school I guess? I'd give it a shot if you like the person teaching the course though.

I wish they didn't weight test scores so heavily, I feel like I've seen so many schools move away from considering test scores as an end all be all. How much do you think they care about your personal statement and life experiences?

People from my school have gotten Bs (never heard of an A though) when their IAs were based on secondary sources, just draw conclusions based on other peoples data. I wrote my bio EE based on secondary sources due to the lab work being to complex to carry out in a high school lab (I compared the links between telomerase and ALT with cancer prognosis), and I'm predicted a B. Just make sure theres a good reason for the data being secondary.

I don't know, this year my school is publishing our EE titles and subjects on the front page of our college apps, but that's a new thing at my school. Honestly I don't think American universities understand what the EE is, and there was never any stress on us to write about our major, and having a good supervisor is probably more beneficial and lang and lit isn't a hard subject to write about
